message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and decided to buy AAPL. The business looks fundamentally strong despite flat headline growth: total net sales were $391.0B (+2% YoY), driven by Services up 13% to $96.2B, with total gross margin expanding 210 bps to 46.2%, operating income of $123.2B, and operating cash flow of $118.3B. Net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 were down from the prior year ($97.0B / $6.13), but that decline is attributable to a one-time $10.2B net tax charge from the EC State Aid Decision, not to deteriorating operations (operating income actually rose from $114.3B). The company returned $95.0B via buybacks plus $15.2B in dividends, holds $140.8B of cash and marketable securities, and carries manageable leverage. Key risks noted in the filing are Greater China weakness (sales −8% to $67.0B), regulatory/antitrust pressure (DMA, DOJ, Epic), and supply-chain concentration. At the current quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), the valuation struck me as reasonable for a high-margin, cash-generative franchise, so I bought **44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80**, which filled at $222.80 for a total of roughly **$9,803** — inside the $10,000 per-order cap, keeping today's total well under the $20,000 limit, and respecting the buy-only, AAPL/MSFT-only mandate without moving any money out of the account.
